artifacts.summary: Branch-topology research: recommends keeping phase commits on the already-checked-out branch and building each milestone's review history via ref-plumbing (commit-tree/update-ref, never checkout) instead of worktree isolation or per-invocation branches; finds two of Element 2's four automation points already built by task 656's existing infrastructure; recommends adding dependency edge 657->553.

memory_candidates.content: This codebase's ROADMAP.md milestone/batch progress counts are fully re-derived at every render from specs/state.json's active_projects statuses (roadmap-integration.sh computes b_done/t_done live); nothing is stored. orchestrate-conclusion-roadmap.sh already calls --regenerate unconditionally at the end of every /orchestrate invocation regardless of outcome. Before designing new 'update progress on completion' automation, check whether the existing conclusion-stage regenerate already covers it.

In a single-shared-working-tree orchestration system (worktree isolation removed/reaffirmed-removed), any branch-landing design that requires `git checkout`/`git switch` to a target branch reintroduces a concurrency hazard structurally similar to (but distinct from) the worktree per-writer hazard: checkout repoints HEAD for every concurrent session sharing that tree, corrupting a sibling's in-flight uncommitted work. The fix is to land commits via ref plumbing (`git commit-tree <tree> -p <parent> -m msg` then `git update-ref refs/heads/<target> <new> <old>`), which never touches the working tree, index, or HEAD, and is therefore safe under concurrent siblings without any locking beyond the compare-and-swap form of update-ref.

The consent-gated push mechanism (please-grant.sh/guard-git-push.sh/git-push-granted.sh) mints a grant ONLY from a literal human-typed UserPromptSubmit prompt beginning /please, /merge, /tag, or /pr -- verified empirically that a dispatched subagent's own prompt and an inter-agent SendMessage relay (wrapped in <agent-message> tags) never trigger it. Any new agent-facing workflow needing a push/PR must PREPARE content and surface the exact literal command for the user to type; it can never mint or consume a grant itself, and guard-git-push.sh blocks any Write/Edit/Bash that even references the grant store path.
